description:
Defk.Build.build!/3 names the cached library by md5 of [cflags, generated C source, priv/defk_runtime.h] and skips cc when `<base>.so` exists in _build/<env>/defk/. The key does not include:
- the ERTS version whose erl_nif.h the library was compiled against (`erts_include/0` resolves it at build time, but it is not hashed);
- the compiler (`CC` env var, default "cc") or its version.

So after an OTP upgrade (or switching asdf/mise versions) without `mix clean`, the stale .so is reused. Loading usually still works because the NIF major version rarely changes, but struct layouts in erl_nif.h have changed across releases before, and a silent reuse of a library built against another header is exactly the class of fault the runtime contract rules out. Switching compilers reuses the other compiler's output too.

Fix: add `:erlang.system_info(:version)` (ERTS version) and the resolved compiler path plus `cc --version` first line (or at least the `CC` value) to the hashed list. Keep the hash prefix at 10 hex chars. Note in the comment above @cflags what the key covers.

Done when: changing the ERTS version or CC produces a different base name (unit test on a hash helper extracted from build!/3), and `mix ci` is green.
title: Build cache key omits the ERTS version and the C compiler
